findings: takeUntilDestroyed called outside injection context — The operator requires injection context but is invoked in ngOnInit. Move the subscription to the constructor or switch to Subject + takeUntil + ngOnDestroy.

Geolocation permission degrades to false instead of unknown — When navigator.permissions is unavailable, the service returns false, making it indistinguishable from explicit denial. Return a third state or document the assumption.

Color equality check is fragile — The template uses estadoGeneral?.color === 'rojo' and 'amarillo' string checks. If a new level is added or color values change, the checks silently break. Use enum or typed accessor.

Mock location refresh with random drift — refrescarUbicacion() adds random coordinate noise instead of fetching real device location. The TODO is present but the mock could mislead users into thinking the feature is implemented.

No error state distinction for contact service failure — If EmergencyContactService.getByUsuario() fails (404, 500, network), the service catches it and returns 0 contacts, which triggers red status. A service error looks identical to zero configured contacts in the UI.

Private user/zone markers could leak on fast navigation — userMarker, zoneCircles, and zoneMarkers are cleaned up in ngOnDestroy, but if the component is destroyed before cargarZonasPeligrosas() completes, the async callback could add markers to a destroyed map.

Missing CSS for new color classes — The template references home-seguridad-item__check--peligro and home-seguridad-item__check--advertencia, and estado-dot--rojo, estado-dot--amarillo, estado-dot--verde. Verify these classes exist in home.scss or the indicators won't render correctly.
